meta.title: AI Acceptable Use — Authorisation and Governance Workflow

steps.title: Training prerequisite check
steps.summary: Before any request is submitted, the requestor must confirm they have completed annual AI risk awareness training. Untrained personnel may not operate AI tools under any tier.
deliverables: Confirmation of current annual AI risk awareness training completion

gates.text: Gate: If training is not current, complete it before proceeding. The ISG team maintains training records.

steps.title: Business case documentation
steps.summary: Document the clear business necessity using the AI Tool Use Case request form. Specify access duration and whether use is single-instance or ongoing. Must be countersigned by a Department Head before submission to ISG.
deliverables: Completed AI Tool Use Case request form, countersigned by Department Head

steps.title: System classification
steps.summary: Classify as Tier 1 (general productivity) or Tier 2 (business-impacting content — marketing, legal, financial, code, translations). The tier drives the depth of due diligence in subsequent steps.
deliverables: Tier assignment documented in the request form

gates.text: Tier 2 gate: Any use case producing marketing, legal, compliance, financial, code, or translation content must follow the full due diligence phase and requires AI Change Board approval.

steps.title: Data identification
steps.summary: Identify all data types to be processed. Determine whether personal data, confidential business information, or Group-identifying data (trade secrets, proprietary code) is involved. This drives tier classification and whether a DPIA is required.
deliverables: Data inventory: types, sensitivity classification, personal/confidential data flag

gates.text: Hard stop: Personal, confidential, or Group-identifying data must not enter external AI tools without approved safeguards and contracts. Escalate to ISG before proceeding.

steps.title: ISG triage decision
steps.summary: ISG reviews the submission and routes it. Not all requests proceed to the AI Change Board — ISG may approve Tier 1 low-risk cases directly. Tier 2 or elevated-risk cases proceed to Phase 2.
deliverables: Routing decision: ISG-level approval OR escalation to Phase 2 due diligence

gates.text: Outcome A: Tier 1, low-risk, no personal/confidential data — ISG approves directly. Proceed to Phase 4 (Record Keeping) and Phase 5 (Ongoing governance).
Outcome B: Tier 2, elevated risk, or personal/confidential data — proceed to Phase 2.

steps.title: Tool fitness evaluation
steps.summary: Before assessing the use case, evaluate whether the AI tool itself is fit for the intended domain. This is a prerequisite to the risk assessment. Covers factual reliability, known bias characteristics, training data provenance and IP exposure, and vendor contractual protections.
deliverables: Tool evaluation report: domain reliability, known bias profile, training data provenance
Vendor assessment: IP indemnity, data processing terms, contractual safeguards
Hallucination risk rating for the intended domain (e.g. legal, medical, financial)

gates.text: Hard stop: If the tool cannot be evaluated or vendor terms are insufficient, the use case must be redesigned around a tool that can be assessed. The risk assessment in Step 7 is only valid if this evaluation is complete.

requirementLabels: AI SR9 — Supply chain / EU AI Act

steps.title: DPIA
steps.summary: Where the use case involves personal data, complete a Data Protection Impact Assessment under GDPR Article 35. Establishes lawful basis, identifies data subjects and special-category data, assesses automated decision-making obligations under Art.22, and documents necessity & proportionality. The DPIA output — particularly the data types inventory — feeds directly into the Risk Assessment in Step 8.
deliverables: Completed DPIA: lawful basis, data subjects, and data types inventory
Special-category data assessment (Art.9) and Art.22 automated decision-making analysis
Necessity & proportionality statement and DPO consultation record
Risk rating and residual risk sign-off

gates.text: Hard stop: If a lawful basis cannot be established, the use case must be rejected or redesigned to eliminate personal data.
Art.22 gate: Where the AI system makes automated decisions with legal or significant effects on data subjects, explicit consent or another Art.22(2) ground must be confirmed before proceeding.

steps.title: Risk assessment
steps.summary: Conduct a formal risk assessment informed by the tool fitness evaluation (Step 6) and the data types identified in the DPIA (Step 7). Risks are grouped by the compliance control framework — covering technical risks (data breaches, cyberattacks, model vulnerabilities), legal risks (GDPR, IP, copyright), and regulatory risks (EU AI Act classification). Each risk is assessed against its attack vectors to determine relevance and priority.
deliverables: Risk register: risks grouped by compliance control area with relevance assessment
Attack vector analysis per risk, informed by DPIA data types
EU AI Act risk classification (prohibited / high-risk / limited-risk / minimal-risk)
Technology Risk Assessment (TRA) where applicable

steps.title: Control identification and disclosure design
steps.summary: Define technical and operational controls to mitigate identified risks. Separately, design transparency and disclosure mechanisms — disclaimer templates, labelling standards, and version control — for Business-Impacting Content. Controls must be specific and verifiable, not delegated to user judgement.
deliverables: Control schedule: encryption, access control, logging, human review checkpoints
Disclosure framework: disclaimer text, internal tagging, version control approach

steps.title: Content verification testing
steps.summary: Structured pre-approval testing of AI-generated output against defined criteria. Evaluates factual accuracy, bias, and IP compliance using the tool fitness evaluation from Step 6 as the baseline. The AI Taskforce conducts checks against documented criteria — not subjective review.
deliverables: Content verification report: accuracy, bias, and IP checks against defined criteria
AI Taskforce sign-off with documented pass/fail criteria

steps.title: AI Change Board approval
steps.summary: Submit the complete authorisation package. The Board reviews the business case, tool fitness evaluation, risk assessment, DPIA (if applicable), control schedule, and content verification evidence. High-risk or prohibited AI systems under the EU AI Act require prior assessment here before any implementation.
deliverables: Submission pack: business case, tool evaluation, RA, DPIA, control schedule, verification report
AI Change Board decision record (approval / conditional / rejection)

gates.text: On approval: Proceed to Phase 4. ISG registers the use case in the central inventory.
On rejection: Requestor notified with documented reasons. Resubmission requires material redesign.

steps.title: Operational controls activation
steps.summary: Before any user accesses the approved tool, the controls defined in Step 9 must be active and verified. This ensures system protections do not evaporate once the workflow ends. Controls are the organisation's responsibility, not the user's.
deliverables: Output logging active and reviewed against logging standards
Human review checkpoints configured for high-stakes content (Tier 2)
Disclosure and labelling templates deployed and tested
Anomaly flagging or output monitoring mechanism in place
Access controls enforced: no Group entity email addresses, MFA required

gates.text: Gate: Tool access must not be granted until all controls from the approved control schedule are confirmed active. Verified by ISG, not self-certified by the requestor.

steps.title: User obligations briefing
steps.summary: Before access is granted, authorised users receive a use-case-specific briefing that tells them exactly what they are responsible for — and what the system is responsible for. User obligations are narrow, behavioural, and achievable. Users are not asked to verify things the system should prevent.
deliverables: Use-case-specific user obligations briefing delivered and acknowledged
System responsibilities schedule communicated to users

system: Bias detection and domain suitability (Steps 6 and 10)
IP and copyright exposure (vendor terms, Step 6)
user: Not inputting data known to be personal, confidential, or classified
Flagging outputs clearly wrong or inconsistent with professional knowledge
Not publishing or acting on output without the required human review step
Deleting chat history after each session as instructed
Reporting anomalous, harmful, or unexpected outputs to ISG

gates.text: Key principle: Users are held to obligations they can actually discharge. Accuracy, bias, and IP verification are organisational controls — not individual responsibilities.

steps.title: Central inventory registration and record keeping
steps.summary: Register the authorised use case in the central inventory. Retain all authorisation records, risk assessments, tool evaluations, and periodic review documentation. TRAs and DPIAs retained outside ISG. AI risks factored into the RCSA process by ExCo.
deliverables: Entry in CISO/ISG central AI tool use case inventory
Retained: business case, tool evaluation, RA, DPIA, Board decision, verification evidence, operational controls schedule

steps.title: Periodic and triggered review
steps.summary: Periodic reviews confirm the business case remains valid, risk assessments are current, operational controls are still active, and the tool fitness evaluation reflects any vendor model updates. Triggered reviews are initiated immediately following security incidents or significant changes.
deliverables: Review schedule at risk-proportionate frequency
Triggered review mechanism active: security incidents, vendor model changes, regulatory updates
Review outcomes: updated tool evaluation, controls verification, SteerCo report

gates.text: Model change trigger: If the vendor updates the underlying model, the tool fitness evaluation (Step 6) must be re-run before continued use is permitted.
Training feedback loop: Trends from reviews must be escalated to ISG for targeted training programmes under AI SR7.
